title: Man dead in Ont. police shooting
article: Ontario\'s Special Investigations Unit is investigating after a 33-year-old man was killed in a police shooting early Wednesday near this village south of Ottawa, police said.
A family member identified the deceased man as Matthew Roke.
Ontario Provincial Police have not confirmed his name.
"There was an interaction between officers and the man, and he was fatally shot by police," said SIU spokeswoman Monica Hudon.
The man died at the scene from injuries.
Hudon would not confirm if the man was armed or if he threatened police.
John Nymann, Roke\'s brother-in-law, said John Roke, the suspect\'s father, and other family members will not comment.
"It\'s a difficult time right now," Nymann said.
At the scene Wednesday morning, a yellow tarp covered the body of the man on the gravel shoulder of the road.
Provincial police first responded to a dispute at around 12:45 a.m., but the man fled into the woods nearby, said Sgt. Kristine Rae.
Officers searched for the man and returned at about 7 a.m. upon receiving a tip the man had returned. That\'s when shots were fired.
The SIU has assigned four investigators and two forensic investigators to the case.
The SIU is an independent provincial agency that investigates "police involved" incidents when civilians are injured or killed.
The shooting happened near a car pool parking lot just north of the village of Maitland, about 100 km south of Ottawa.
